Q1.text: You are given a difficult problem for which your teacher has not provided a standard method. What would you most naturally do first?
options: Think about it independently and develop my own approach.
Search for examples of how similar problems have been solved.
Discuss it with classmates and compare approaches.
Start experimenting and see what happens.

Q2.text: Suppose you are learning about artificial intelligence. Which part would interest you most?
options: Understanding the theory and principles behind AI.
Seeing how AI is used in real-world applications.
Trying an AI tool and experimenting with what it can do.
Discussing how AI could affect society and people's lives.

Q3.text: Your team must choose between two project ideas. One is safer and more likely to succeed; the other is more ambitious but uncertain. What would you most likely consider first?
options: Which option has stronger evidence and logic.
Which option the team members feel more comfortable with.
Whether we can combine the strengths of both options.
Whether the ambitious option is worth taking the risk.

Q4.text: You have three major assignments, coaching/classes and an upcoming examination in the same week. Which approach sounds most like you?
options: Create a detailed timetable and follow it.
Set priorities but adjust the plan as circumstances change.
Complete whichever task feels most urgent at the time.
Work intensely when deadlines become closer.

Q5.text: After spending a full day at school, which situation would generally make you feel more refreshed?
options: Spending time talking or doing something with friends.
Working on something that personally interests me.

Q6.text: You spend several days preparing a project and receive a much lower evaluation than expected. What would be your most natural response?
options: Analyse exactly where I went wrong.
Ask the evaluator or teacher for detailed feedback.
Feel disappointed but try a different approach next time.
Move on quickly and focus on the next task.

Q7.text: On a scale of 1–10, how comfortable are you with making an important decision without simply following what your friends or family expect you to do?

Q10.text: Your school gives you ₹10,000 to develop one project. What would you prefer?
options: Develop a structured system for managing the project and its finances.

Q22.text: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3:2. If there are 45 boys, how many girls are there?
Q22.explanation: 3:2 ratio means 45 boys = 3 parts, so 1 part = 15, girls = 2 parts = 30

Q23.text: All engineers are problem-solvers. Some problem-solvers are entrepreneurs. Which statement must be true?
Q23.explanation: All engineers are problem-solvers (definitely true). The second statement doesn't determine if any engineers are entrepreneurs.

Q24.text: Find the next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ___

Q25.text: Every researcher studies evidence. Priya is a researcher. What must be true?
Q25.explanation: Deductive reasoning: If all researchers study evidence, and Priya is a researcher, then Priya studies evidence.

Q53.text: Your marks suddenly fall in a subject you normally perform well in. What would you do first?
options: Analyse what changed in my preparation or understanding.
Talk to my teacher about the problem.
Discuss it with someone I trust.
Give myself some time and then try again.

Q54.text: A close friend disagrees strongly with your opinion. What would you most likely do?
options: Explain why I think I am correct.
Try to understand why they see it differently.
Look for evidence that could help both of us understand the issue.

Q55.text: You have several important tasks and begin feeling overwhelmed. Which response is most likely?
options: Break the work into smaller priorities.
Take a short break and return with a clearer mind.
Ask someone for help or guidance.
Continue working and hope I catch up.

A system combining several of these ideas.

options: Generate several possible solutions before choosing one.
Combine existing ideas into something new.

Q59.text: Your first solution fails. What does this situation make you want to do?
options: Ask others to challenge my thinking.
Start again using what I learned.

Q79.instruction: Type or select up to THREE alternative career choices
Q79.responseFormat: Free text or multi-select - up to 3 careers
